title: Pinned runtime semver + coordinated upgrade hooks for runtime/API/SDK/Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a coordinated approach that pins runtime semantic versions for customer-facing LTS channels and provides automated upgrade hooks across the runtime, REST API, client SDKs, and Console. Goal is to minimize unexpected behavioral changes during upgrades while enabling safe, automated rollouts and fast rollbacks when SLOs regress.
acceptance_criteria: A clear semver contract exists for runtime artifacts and documented mapping to API surface compatibility (major/minor/patch semantics)
An automated preflight suite runs for each candidate upgrade covering: API contract tests, SDK smoke tests, console integration flows, and KV cache backward-compatibility checks
Deployment orchestration supports staged rollouts (canary -> cohort -> worldwide) with configurable health gates (latency P95, error rate, cost spike thresholds)
Automatic rollback triggers are implemented and exercised in dry-run: threshold breach causes rollback within the deployment pipeline and notifies stakeholders
Upgrade hooks are implemented as idempotent tasks (migrations/feature-flags toggles) and exposed to Dedicated/Private customers as opt-in rollouts
Documentation and customer-facing release notes are autogenerated from validated changelogs and include a compatibility matrix for runtime/API/SDK/Console
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, API, SDK, and Console leads. Agreed constraints: no breaking changes in LTS-major, minor releases may include opt-in features behind flags.

2025-02-15: Drafted semver policy in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Semver+and+LTS+Policy (internal). Feedback from PM: include clear migration path for cache format changes.
2025-02-18: Prototype preflight runner completed (alpha) that runs integration smoke tests against canary cluster. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-preflight/pull/12
2025-02-21: Design review with Security and SRE. Security requested explicit KMS compatibility check for Private deployments — added to preflight checklist.

2025-02-25: Trade-off discussion: strict semver pinning reduces customer surprise but increases number of pinned variants we must support. Decided to support pinned-major + pinned-minor lanes for next 12 months.
2025-03-01: Implemented rollout gate definitions in orchestration service (canary-size, gate-duration, metrics thresholds). Initial gate: P95 latency < 250ms and error rate < 0.5% over 15m
2025-03-03: PM review: asked for autogenerated release notes and a clear deprecation timeline UI in Console. Logged follow-up ticket for Console UX: PM-4720

2025-03-05: Ran first dry-run upgrade on staging with synthetic traffic. Canary passed, cohort failed due to SDK compatibility issue; rollback automation executed successfully and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/240
notes: Decision: LTS channels will map to pinned-major (three year support) and pinned-minor (12 months) tracks; patch updates remain fully backward compatible and auto-deployed
Preflight checklist items: API contract checker, SDK generated-client smoke test, console e2e happy path, KV cache decode test, KMS key rotation validation (for Private)
Rollback action sequence: immediate traffic shift to previous release cohort -> trigger schema/shim revert if applied -> notify pager and run postmortem workflow
Customers on Dedicated may opt into faster minor channel via console toggle; Private customers get a Terraform/config marker to opt-in
We will publish a machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV/JSON) alongside release notes to drive automation in customers' CI
